How to automatically generate "49 tags that perfectly match the image" using MidStock's image analysis
When generating images for Adobe Stock with Midjourney, do you ask AI like ChatGPT to "create the title and tags for submission at the same time as the prompt!"?
While this method may seem efficient at first glance, it actually has a major pitfall in the stock photo industry.
That is the problem that the content instructed in the prompt and the actual content of the image output by Midjourney do not necessarily match.
In this article, I will explain, along with actual screens, why the "feature to generate a title and 49 tags from a completed image" included in the iOS/Android app 'MidStock' that I developed is directly linked to improving the review pass rate and the number of downloads.
■ The discrepancy that occurs when you "create prompts and metadata at the same time"
When using Midjourney, it is common for elements written in the prompt to be omitted, or conversely, for small items not specified to be drawn.
For example, suppose you created 49 tags at the same time when creating the prompt, assuming a "dinner with a wine glass, bread, and vegetables."
However, what if the best image that actually came out of Midjourney did not have a wine glass or bread, but instead had a "candle" and a "wooden spoon" drawn in them?
If you use the tags from when you created the prompt as they are, the following negative effects will occur.
・Tags that do not exist in the image (wine, bread) are mixed in, leading to Adobe Stock review rejections or lower evaluations in search algorithms
・Attractive elements actually drawn (candles, wooden spoons, specific types of vegetables) are missing from the tags, so they do not show up in buyer searches
In other words, to create accurate metadata that actually sells, you need to "show the finished image directly to the AI and reverse-engineer the tags from what is depicted," rather than "creating tags from the prompt."
■ Demonstration: Creating "perfectly matching metadata" from a single finished image
Now, I will show you how accurately metadata can be created from a generated image using the "Image Analysis" feature of "MidStock."
The image we will analyze this time is this illustration of a warm dining table.
On the plate are three types of roasted vegetables, next to it is wooden cutlery, in the back are a candle and a cup, and slightly visible in the background, rather than the foreground, is a person's clothing.
▼ Step 1: Select the finished image in the "Image Analysis" tab
Open the "Image Analysis" tab at the bottom of the app, select the image saved on your smartphone, and tap "Analyze one image at once" (multiple images can also be selected and analyzed in bulk).
Tapping will start the AI visual analysis.
▼ Step 2: Title and category completed by reading every corner of the image
Once the analysis is complete, the created metadata is saved in the "Library" tab.
・Japanese Title: Plate of roasted vegetable dishes lined up on a dining table lit by candles
・English Title: Plate of Roasted Vegetables on Dining Table with Candlelight
Not only is the main subject of roasted vegetables accurately reflected in the title, but the situation of the "dining table lit by candles" is as well.
▼ Step 3: 49 tags that perfectly match the ingredients and accessories depicted
Scroll down the screen further to see the 49 automatically generated tag keywords.
・English tags (top excerpts): #roasted vegetables #dinner table #beetroot #carrot #potato #food #candle #plate #cutlery #dining #tablecloth #vegetarian #healthy #meal #wooden spoon ...
・Japanese tags (in order of priority, 49 items): Roasted vegetables, dining table, beetroot, carrot, potato, food, candle, plate, cutlery, dinner, tablecloth, vegetarian, healthy, meal, wooden spoon, fork, napkin, cup, pottery, candlestick, flame, candle...
This is the most important point to note.
Because the AI is looking directly at the actual image, it doesn't just settle for calling the vegetables on the plate 'vegetables,' but accurately identifies them one by one as 'beetroot,' 'carrot,' and 'potato.'
Furthermore, the 49 tags are filled with elements actually present in the image, including the 'wooden spoon,' 'fork,' and 'napkin' placed on the right, the 'pottery cup' and 'candlestick/candle' in the background, and even keywords for the atmosphere and seasonal feel like 'autumn/winter' and 'cozy.'
▼ Step 4: Supports art style determination and 'fine-tuning by looking at the image'
If you scroll further to the bottom, you will also be automatically guided through settings that are often confusing when submitting to Adobe Stock.
・Content created with generative AI tools: Yes
・Identifiable people or property: No (People: No, Property: No)
Since this image was not a photograph but had an anime/illustration-style touch, the AI detected the art style and automatically determined the file format as 'Illustration.' It also accurately judged that the person in the background, whose face is not identifiable because only part of their clothing is visible, means 'Identifiable people: No,' and guides you accordingly.
Even if you want to 'strengthen specific keywords a little more,' you can easily brush them up at any time using the 'Fine-tune by looking at the image' or 'Re-analyze' buttons at the bottom.
■ Straight to submission with CSV export and SFTP transfer
Once the accurate title and 49 tags are complete, you can proceed directly to the submission process using the 'Export / SFTP Transfer' button on the bottom right.
・Light Plan (300 yen/month): Unlimited prompt generation & metadata generation from images

・Premium Plan (1,100 yen/month): Supports direct metadata embedding into image files & vector (SVG) conversion
※Note: To use the AI features of this app, you need to set your own AI API key (such as Google's Gemini API or OpenAI API). By using your own API key, the API cost remains around a few dozen yen even if you analyze hundreds of images (you can also utilize free tiers), and the app itself is offered at an affordable price starting from 300 yen per month.

The applications and their source code are available through Thomas’s GitHub repositories.
Thomas describes the software as clean-room implementations, meaning the applications are intended to reproduce functionality without copying Adobe’s proprietary source code. That remains the developer’s characterization rather than an independently verified legal assessment.
The project targets macOS, Windows, and Linux, although compatibility and available features may vary by application.
How well do the free Adobe alternatives work?
ArtCraft’s most recognizable feature is its resemblance to Adobe’s interfaces.
AppleInsider tested PhotoCraft and found a familiar layout, including editing tools, icons, and a layers panel resembling Photoshop.
However, the similarities do not necessarily extend to the underlying functionality.
In separate testing, TechRadar reported problems with PhotoCraft’s HEIC image support and file-saving options. Its review also identified limitations in FilmCraft, including missing or incomplete video-editing functions.
These shortcomings matter for professionals who depend on reliable editing tools, consistent file handling, and compatibility with existing projects.
For now, the applications remain experimental, and independent testing has not established that they can replace Adobe’s software in demanding production workflows.
ArtCraft’s significance extends beyond the possibility of free creative software.
With Claude assisting in development, Thomas has built applications resembling products that typically require considerable programming effort.The project illustrates how AI coding assistants can help developers create interfaces, prototype features, and refine software without manually writing every component.
However, the limitations identified in early testing reveal an important distinction between building software quickly and making it dependable.
A convincing interface may be relatively straightforward to reproduce, but professional applications also require reliable file handling, accurate output, and consistent performance across different workflows.
That distinction matters for businesses evaluating AI-generated software. Development speed may reduce the effort needed to produce an initial application, but it does not eliminate the work required to test, secure, maintain, and support it.
ArtCraft offers a visible example of that trade-off. Its applications demonstrate the possibilities of AI-assisted development while showing why functional completeness remains a challenge.

Could AI-built software challenge subscription tools?
ArtCraft also raises questions about how AI-assisted development could affect competition in the software market.
Thomas has cited frustration with Adobe’s subscription and cancellation practices as part of his motivation for creating free alternatives. By helping smaller developers build recognizable applications, AI coding tools could lower some of the barriers to entering markets dominated by established software providers.
However, competing with Adobe involves more than reproducing its interface or basic editing features.
Businesses rely on file compatibility, technical support, ongoing updates, and established workflows. These factors can make switching software costly even when an alternative is free.
Thomas has already extended his approach beyond Adobe, developing open-source applications inspired by Microsoft Word, Excel, and PowerPoint, according to Tom’s Hardware.
For IT leaders, the development highlights a potential shift in software purchasing decisions. As AI makes it easier to build alternatives, organizations may have more options, but they will still need to weigh cost savings against reliability, security, and long-term support.
ArtCraft may not be ready to replace Adobe Creative Cloud, but it raises a question for businesses: as AI makes software easier to build, what will make it worth paying for?

The 24/7 Wall St. price target remains at $294.54, with a buy rating and 90% confidence. Valuation is the deciding factor.

The apps have virtually all of the same menus and workflows

LightCraft is the Lightroom equivalent, and it's modeled on the cloud-based Lightroom rather than Lightroom Classic. Can anyone explain to me how this process isn't software piracy?
The idea of a clean room implementation relies on multiple human actors. One team writing specs and another totally different team reading them.
This is one team running a tool against a binary, then running that same tool against the product of the first run. That not even remotely close to a clean room implementation.
The problem is that we're not really set up legally to handle this. Creating software used to require a fair amount of skill just to get something which worked and most people with that skill weren't just going to do the incredibly tedious work of taking someone else's program, mapping out exactly how every bit of it worked, and writing their own code to do exactly the same thing. Copying was either copying source (which copyright law clearly covers) or at the level of ideas and concepts which copyright doesn't really cover: in Apple v. Microsoft and HP in the 90s, it was an established fact that Microsoft Windows added features which Mac OS had years before but Apple lost all but one of the claims because the court didn't agree that Apple could claim the broader GUI concepts as opposed to very narrow implementations (the one claim they got was that HP's trash can looked too much like the Mac's, which is one reason why Windows uses a recycling bin).
So that left most of the industry with two common paths: bottom feeders would copy code illegally but were relatively easily caught as well because the code was so similar (e.g. in the QuickTime / Video for Windows suit, it was exactly the same code used by an unethical contractor and Microsoft quickly removed it because it was completely unambiguously not their code) or there's a broad conceptual inspiration but the underlying code is relatively different except where there are domain similarities (e.g. a JPEG decoder will have a lot of terms with the same names due to implementing the same spec and the underlying math has to be the same). This wasn't perfect but it kept the problem at a manageable level because the people with the skills to clone things usually could do more valuable things and larger businesses knew they'd get caught (back when the DOJ enforced laws) so you had some problems like the guys who'd download games from the Play/App Store, repackage them, and change enough of the visible assets not to be caught, but those were small scale operations because it's straightforward to analyze compiled binaries and show the underlying structure is highly similar. There wasn't enough money to be made in the confusion / knock-off market to support hiring more / better-skilled people to do a better job cloning big apps or keeping up with new developments.
AI changes that because you can task an LLM with all of the tedious work of mapping out how the original app works, generating code to mimic that behavior, and while it's still going to require a fair amount of work to correctly implement functionality and correct confabulations, it's still a lot more feasible for a one person project than it would have been 5 years ago. LLMs also tirelessly repeat that process with each release so the upstream can't rely on moving faster than a single knock-off artist can keep up.
Again, none of this is perfect and getting anywhere near the same level of quality (even for Adobe/Microsoft levels) is going to take time but it's reducing the number of people needed considerably and especially reducing the skill level. For example, the number of people who could create a game's code, artwork, and sound on their own is a relatively small group compared to the number of people who could, say, have a coding agent handle a lot of the code and an image/audio generator fill in the gaps instead of hiring artists and voice actors, and the lower end mobile / Steam market makes it hard for small players to stand out in search results compared to the number of people who are going to search for Photoshop but use anything else (i.e. their class / boss gives them a copy).
I think this is going to hurt smaller indie developers first because they don't have the massive name recognition and legal departments which Adobe or Microsoft have and the resource levels are more comparable: the small indie team has to spend a lot of time developing the concept & behavior for an app so if they have, say, a 5-10 person company they're not as well positioned to stay ahead of a small 1-2 person clone shop which doesn't have to do the hard R&D.

Chapter 1: Summary of the video's claims — What was discussed
The core of this video is that a group called ArtCraft used Claude's Opus 5.5 to rebuild the Adobe product suite from scratch and release it for free.
Seven pieces of software were released. The Photoshop alternative is "PhotoCraft", the Premiere alternative is "FilmCraft," and the After Effects alternative is "EffectCraft." Furthermore, they have "VectorCraft" as an Illustrator alternative, "DesignCraft" as an InDesign alternative, "LightCraft" as a Lightroom alternative, and even "PDFCraft" as an Acrobat alternative.
The implementation language is Rust, and it is explained that they were "clean-room reimplemented" using Opus 5.5. In other words, the claim is that they did not disassemble or analyze (reverse engineer) existing Adobe software, but rather rewrote it from scratch by looking only at the functional specifications. This is cited as the basis for why it is legally clear.
The release location is getartcraft.com/apps, and the code can also be obtained from GitHub (github.com/storytold). PhotoCraft reportedly gained 20,000 stars just a few hours after its release. In the video, demos of actually operating PhotoCraft and FilmCraft were shown, introducing how many elements that people who usually use Adobe products would find "familiar," such as layer styles, timeline zoom functions, and shortcut keys, have been reproduced.
What is important here is the point that this does not end as just a "free clone festival." In the latter half of the video, there is a discussion about how these software programs are designed on the premise that they will be operated directly by AI agents, especially Claude.
Specifically, a CLI (command-line interface) is built into each piece of software, and a Markdown file called "agents.md" is provided. This is like an operation handbook for agents, and by having agents like Claude read this, they can understand the functions and operation methods of each software and proceed with tasks autonomously.
In the video, a demo was actually shown where an entire animation with layers was generated just by throwing a single prompt at EffectCraft (the After Effects alternative). It also showed how a magazine spread layout is created by Claude in DesignCraft (the InDesign alternative).
The conclusion that can be drawn: The core of this video is that this release is not just about "free Adobe," but is designed as an experimental ground for AI agents to directly operate creative software.
Chapter 2: Interpretation from my own industry experience
2-1. How this hits home in current practical work
Many people use image editing and video editing software in marketing and side-hustle settings, but honestly, Adobe's subscription costs are not a small burden. Even Photoshop alone costs several thousand yen per month, and the Creative Cloud complete plan is even higher. For sole proprietors and freelancers, this fixed cost hits surprisingly hard, like a body blow.
What this ArtCraft release shows is the possibility that the "value of the tool itself" is starting to decline relatively. As mentioned in the video, much of what can be done in Photoshop was reproduced with considerable accuracy in just a few weeks of development and a few days of release. Of course, there is a disclaimer that it is not a perfect replica, but it cannot be overlooked that it is at a level that can cover the majority of daily editing tasks.
However, what we should be calm about here is that a simple judgment of "switching because it's free" is premature. If you are using it for business, you need to judge it including factors such as compatibility, support systems, and integration with existing files. I think it is appropriate to view this as a stage where "options have increased."
Although not mentioned in the video, I felt that this could become a kind of "insurance" for people who take on video editing as a side hustle.
For example, situations where your Premiere license suddenly expires during client work, or the timing for paying high renewal fees doesn't align, are common in practice. In such cases, an open-source version like FilmCraft could function as a "temporary substitute." Of course, it is high-risk to suddenly use it for production in a professional setting, but there should be plenty of room to consider it for rough cuts or testing purposes.
Also, the fact that it supports agent operations is an interesting implication from a practical standpoint. Software that comes standard with an "AI operation manual" like agents.md is a sign that "ease of integration with AI" will become one of the evaluation criteria for selecting business tools in the future. This may be an element that will also be required for Adobe products themselves.
Conclusion: Beyond being free, the realization from a practical perspective is that "whether it is designed to be easily handled by AI" is becoming a new standard for choosing tools.
Chapter 3: Perspectives not covered in the video
3-1. Counterarguments and alternative cases
The video explained that it is "legal because it is a clean-room re-implementation," but this was merely introduced as the creator's claim. The video did not touch upon how Adobe would actually react or how the similarity in trademarks and the appearance of features would be judged.
Since the video mentioned the name PhotoCraft and the high degree of reproduction of layer styles, the boundary between "imitation of functionality" and "imitation of appearance/experience" may become a topic of debate in the future. The video remained optimistic about this point throughout, but I think it is healthy for the reader to understand that "this is an issue that has not yet been settled."
Another point often overlooked is the instability behind the speed of being released within hours to days. The video also included the statement, "Of course, it's not a perfect replica, after all, it was released 24 hours ago." In other words, one must not forget the premise that this is software that has not yet matured (is not stable).
The expectation that improvements will proceed in an open-source and community-driven manner was also discussed in the video, but that also means "there is no support system at this time." The video did not emphasize that if you adopt it for full-scale business use, bug handling and preparation for data loss risks are your own responsibility.
Conclusion: I think the way to read it without being swept away by the enthusiasm of the video is to evaluate it with the premise that both legality and quality are "still in development at this time."
4-1. Concrete actions you can take starting tomorrow
Access getartcraft.com/apps, and first download one software you are interested in (such as PhotoCraft or FilmCraft) for free and try it out.
Instead of using production data, check "how much it reproduces" in your usual workflow using light test materials.
Confirm the existence of agents.md and try instructing an agent like Claude to perform simple editing tasks (text changes, layer adjustments, etc.).
The idea discussed in the video of "AI for the first draft, manual work for the finishing touches" can be applied directly to practical work. For example, for SNS banner images or simple logo animations, it is suitable to send a prompt to Claude and have it create a rough first draft on EffectCraft or PhotoCraft. The video also pointed out that "if it's a logo animation, it can be made sufficiently with a video generation model," but it was stated that for long-form editing work that requires layer management, it is more efficient to have Claude create the first draft with these tools.
On the other hand, for final deliverables for clients or work where you want to be particular about the details of color and placement, the conclusion of the video is that the process of humans moving their hands to make fine adjustments cannot be omitted. From the statement that "fine adjustments are much easier if you are well-versed in the tool," I feel that the realistic compromise is a division of labor where humans polish the first draft created by AI, rather than leaving everything to AI.
Conclusion: If you assume a division of roles where "AI does the first draft and humans do the finishing touches," there is plenty of room to incorporate even free tools into practical work.

For Salesforce, Cramer built on the earlier comments we've linked above. He extended his take to outline that Salesforce was sticky with businesses and was making durable inroads into businesses. For Adobe, a major victim of the AI wave, the fact that management also outlined that AI-first ARR grew by 150% indicated that the firm might be improving reslience against the emerging technology.
Looking at the valuation, Salesforce, through its forward P/E ratio of 27.78 is more richly valued than Adobe, which trades at 8.73. With Adobe's historic range being 25x and 45x, the market appears to be pricing in an extreme disruption. Additionally, while the ratio implies a yield of 11.45%, this could very well be a value trap. For Salesforce, it suggests that the market is quite optimistic. ADOBE: U.S. HOLIDAY SHOPPING SEASON TO HIT RECORD $275.1 BILLION ONLINE, RISING 6.7% YOY

Adobe (Nasdaq: ADBE) released today its online shopping forecast for the 2026 holiday season, covering the period from Nov. 1 to Dec. 31, 2026. Based on Adobe Analytics data, the analysis provides the most comprehensive view into U.S. e-commerce by analyzing direct transactions online. Adobe's forecast is based on over 1 trillion visits to U.S. retail sites, 100 million SKUs and 18 product categories—more than any other technology company or research organization. Adobe Analytics is part of Adobe CX Enterprise, relied upon by global brands to accelerate Customer Experience Orchestration, connecting data, content and AI to deliver real-time, personalized interactions.
2026 holidays set to cross $275 billion milestone, with pre-season spending uptick in October
Adobe expects U.S. online sales to hit $275.1 billion this holiday season (Nov. 1 to Dec. 31, 2026), growing 6.7% year-over-year (YoY). Cyber Week (the five-day period between Thanksgiving and Cyber Monday) is set to drive $47.5 billion online (up 7.4% YoY), representing 17.3% of the full holiday season spend.
Cyber Monday (Nov. 30) is expected to set a new milestone for U.S. e-commerce, with consumers spending over $15 billion online in a single day ($15.1 billion, up 6.2% YoY). The second biggest day of the season will be Black Friday ($12.9 billion, up 9.2% YoY), which is growing faster than Cyber Monday—driven in part by having the biggest discounts for categories such as TVs, apparel and appliances. Thanksgiving is set to drive $6.9 billion (up 8.5% YoY), bolstered by impulse shopping: A record 63% of online spend is set to come through mobile devices (up from 61.6% in 2025), outpacing the full season where mobile will account for 57.4% of overall spend (up from 56.4% in 2025).
Of the full holiday season spend, electronics ($63.3 billion, up 5.9% YoY) and apparel ($51.3 billion, up 4.7% YoY) remain tentpole categories in e-commerce, but consumers are also embracing other categories online with stronger growth observed in furniture ($33.4 billion, up 7.3% YoY), grocery ($26.1 billion, up 10.3% YoY), toys ($9.6 billion, up 9.6% YoY) and cosmetics ($9.2 billion, 9.5% YoY).
Pre-season shopping in October continues to accelerate
The Prime Day event in October (which became an annual tradition in 2022) has become an industrywide e-commerce moment, with discounts happening broadly across U.S. retailers. It is now driving significant consumer spend in advance of the holiday season. Adobe expects $95.8 billion will be spent online in October 2026, up a notable 8% YoY. Nearly $10 billion will be spent during the Prime Day event from October 6 to 7 ($9.9 billion, up 9.2% YoY), driven in part by discounts that are set to peak at 19% off listed price. This has changed the shape of the holiday season, pushing U.S. retailers to manage promotions and inventory effectively to capture an additional pre-season spike in shopping interest.
Consumers expected to take advantage of strong discounts to stock up on essentials
Adobe expects competitive discounts this holiday season, up to 30% off listed price (during Cyber Week). Shoppers will see deals throughout the season, up to 14% in early November, up to 21% just before Thanksgiving and up to 10-15% throughout December.

During Cyber Week, online sales of personal hygiene products are expected to jump 150% (compared to average sales levels in September 2026) and clothing basics by 210%. Other essentials set to see a boost include baby products (up 113%), pet products (up 93%) and household cleaning items (up 49%).
Buy Now Pay Later to drive over $21 billion in holiday season spend
The flexible payment method continues to see traction amongst consumers during the holiday season. Buy Now Pay Later (BNPL) is expected to drive $21.3 billion (Nov-Dec), up 6.6% YoY. Usage is set to spike on Cyber Monday, where BNPL will be used for $1.09 billion in online spend. This is the second consecutive year where over a billion dollars were driven by BNPL on Cyber Monday. On Black Friday, BNPL is set to drive $807 million in online spend. Most of BNPL spend will come through mobile devices (82% share vs. desktop), showing the impact of impulse shopping on driving adoption of the payment method.
Another AI-powered holiday season: In the 2024 holiday season, Adobe observed the first uptick in consumers using AI-powered chat and browser services for online shopping (from finding deals to quickly locating products). Adobe expects AI traffic to U.S. retail sites this holiday season (measured by shoppers clicking on a link) to rise 130% YoY. The biggest uptick is expected on Thanksgiving (up 159% YoY), followed by Black Friday (up 95% YoY) and Cyber Monday (up 88% YoY). In an Adobe survey* of 5,000 consumers, 77% of respondents who have used AI for online shopping report feeling more confident in their purchase, and 69% say they are less likely to return an item they bought.
Hot sellers: Top gaming consoles this season are expected to include Nintendo Switch 2, Sony PlayStation 5/Pro and Xbox Series X, along with games such as Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 4, EA SPORTS FC 27, Grand Theft Auto VI, Madden NFL 27, Marvel's Wolverine, Minecraft Dungeons II, NBA 2K27 and Pokémon Pokopia. Social media and affiliates drive purchase behavior: Adobe measures the impact of different marketing investments during the holiday season, looking at its contribution to revenue. Affiliates/partners (which includes social influencers) and social media overall are set to see the biggest gains in share of revenue, up 12% and 17%, respectively. In comparison, paid search is expected to rise by 4%. Within the affiliates/partner category, cashback and rewards partners leads in affiliate traffic with a 36% share, followed by influencers and creators at 22%. Adobe and NVIDIA Expand Collaboration to Speed Agentic Creation
Thu, October 15, 2026 at 12:00 PM CDT 7 min read
Adobe is expanding its collaboration with NVIDIA to optimize its flagship tools including Adobe Photoshop, Premiere, Substance 3D, Frame.io and Brand Concierge, delivering faster AI-powered creation, production and personalization.
Adobe is bringing the power of the NVIDIA RTX Spark superchip to its agentic creative applications Photoshop, Premiere and Substance 3D. Optimized to take full advantage of RTX Spark, these applications deliver up to 2x faster AI processing, editing, color and effects, helping creatives iterate faster and stay in their creative flow.

SAN JOSE, Calif., October 15, 2026--(BUSINESS WIRE)--Adobe (Nasdaq: ADBE), the global technology leader that unleashes creativity, productivity and customer experiences through innovative tools and platforms, and NVIDIA today announced an expansion of their partnership to optimize Adobe's flagship tools including Adobe Photoshop, Premiere, Substance 3D, Frame.io and Brand Concierge, delivering faster AI-powered creation, production and personalization.
This work builds on Adobe and NVIDIA's strategic partnership announced in March, which brings together Adobe's creative and marketing workflows, models and technology with NVIDIA's open models, libraries, research and accelerated computing to accelerate creative, production and marketing workflows across video, images, 3D and other creative media. That collaboration includes GPU acceleration for media ingestion and intelligence in Frame.io, as well as ongoing work around Adobe Substance 3D, Adobe Firefly Foundry and 3D digital twin workflows for enterprise customers.
"Creative workflows are more multimodal than ever, with many projects spanning images, video, audio, motion and 3D, making performance critical to helping creatives stay focused on their ideas and craft," said Deepa Subramaniam, vice president, product marketing, creative professionals, Adobe. "By partnering with NVIDIA to optimize Photoshop, Premiere and Substance 3D for RTX Spark and accelerating Frame.io in the cloud, we're delivering the performance creatives need to bring their ideas to life."
"AI agents are helping creators unlock deeper and richer workflows using the Adobe applications they know and love," said Jason Paul, vice president, local AI, NVIDIA. "Powered by RTX Spark, Adobe's optimized tools deliver up to 2x faster performance to accelerate these new workflows."
Empowering Creatives With Faster Adobe Tools Rearchitected With NVIDIA
Creative professionals today move between image, video, motion and 3D, sometimes all within the same project. As AI increasingly becomes part of the creative process, they need technology that keeps pace with the speed of their ideas and the complexity of their workflows. As an industry leader in creativity, Adobe's tools apply decades of creative expertise to amplify human potential and make it easier to quickly turn ideas into impactful work.
Adobe is bringing the power of the NVIDIA RTX Spark superchip, which NVIDIA launched earlier this month, to its agentic creative applications Photoshop, Premiere and Substance 3D. RTX-accelerated and optimized to take full advantage of RTX Spark's unified memory and AI compute, these applications deliver up to 2x faster AI processing, editing, color and effects, helping creatives iterate faster and stay in their creative flow.
Adobe rearchitected Photoshop around GPU-accelerated compositing to be faster and more responsive for creative tasks from removing distractions with the Remove Tool to applying effects like Gaussian Blur and Light Leaks directly on canvas.
Some of the most demanding post-production workflows in Premiere, from playback and rendering, to effects, color and AI-powered tools, are RTX-accelerated and optimized for RTX Spark. This results in real, tangible speed gains for popular audio and video features in Premiere like Enhance Speech and Object Mask. For 3D artists using Substance 3D Painter, RTX Spark speeds up the heaviest steps around texturing.
Accelerating Cloud Video Workflows With Frame.io and NVIDIA
Adobe is also using NVIDIA accelerated computing to speed cloud media processing and intelligent content discovery for Adobe Frame.io, helping production teams find and use growing media libraries faster. The updated Frame.io pipeline uses NVIDIA video acceleration, including NVIDIA NVDEC for hardware-accelerated decoding and NVIDIA TensorRT ™ with CUDA™ for content preprocessing and embedding generation.
Moving compute-intensive video decoding, preprocessing and embedding generation onto NVIDIA GPUs lets Frame.io process media faster and make it searchable sooner, while supporting more responsive discovery across large content libraries.
Early performance results from selected Frame.io transcode and search workloads show:
Approximately 5x faster embedding generation
4-5x improvement in P95 processing latency
An approximately 80% smaller search proxy
For creative teams, these gains mean uploaded content becomes searchable sooner, larger libraries refresh more efficiently, and discovery and review stay frictionless as media volumes grow.
Personalized Conversational Experiences With Adobe Brand Concierge Optimized On NVIDIA Nemotron
Brands also want more choice and value from the AI models powering personalized experiences. Open models can help meet that need, providing a flexible and efficient way to deliver high-quality, responsive conversations at enterprise scale.
Adobe and NVIDIA worked together to optimize Brand Concierge using NVIDIA Nemotron™ open models. This version will be available to enterprise customers later this year. NVIDIA has also selected Brand Concierge to drive personalized conversational experiences grounded in organizational data and content. This enables NVIDIA to tailor interactions on their website based on customer needs, while leveraging Nemotron to deliver fast, high-quality responses at scale.
Get ready for what's next — with three days of creative skill-building, visionary keynotes and valuable connections at Adobe MAX, running Nov. 10-12. Adobe and NVIDIA will showcase the latest advancements for creators alongside their hardware partners.

• Adobe AI-first ARR grew more than 150% year over year
• Achieves major milestone of 1 billion monthly active users (MAU) across creativity and productivity solutions
SAN JOSE, Calif. – Sept. 10, 2026 – Adobe (Nasdaq:ADBE), the global technology leader that unleashes creativity and productivity for individuals and businesses through innovative platforms and tools, today reported financial results for its third quarter FY2026 ended Aug. 28, 2026.
“Adobe delivered record Q3 results, reflecting the strength of our AI innovation, expanding customer reach and leadership across creativity, productivity and customer experience,” said Shantanu Narayen, chair and CEO, Adobe. “Reaching a landmark of more than one billion monthly active users is a defining moment for Adobe, and I have confidence that Anil will build on this momentum to drive Adobe's next chapter of growth and innovation in the AI era.”
“Adobe delivered double-digit revenue and EPS growth in Q3 and we're raising full year revenue and EPS targets,” said Steve Day, senior vice president and interim CFO, Adobe. “We are expanding our user base through a freemium strategy and deepening engagement with agentic experiences to deliver long-term durable growth.”
Third Quarter FY2026 Financial Highlights
•Adobe achieved record revenue of $6.76 billion in its third quarter of FY2026, which represents 13% year-over-year growth, or 12% in constant currency. Diluted earnings per share was $4.62 on a GAAP basis and $6.13 on a non-GAAP basis.
•Total Adobe Annualized Recurring Revenue (“ARR”) exiting the quarter was $27.50 billion.
•GAAP operating income in the third quarter was $2.35 billion and non-GAAP operating income was $2.97 billion. GAAP net income was $1.83 billion and non-GAAP net income was $2.42 billion.
•Record Q3 cash flows from operations were $2.52 billion.
•Exiting the quarter, Remaining Performance Obligations (“RPO”) were $22.16 billion, and Current Remaining Performance Obligations (“cRPO”) were 67%.
•Adobe repurchased approximately 9.5 million shares during the quarter.
Third Quarter FY2026 Customer Group Highlights
•Total Customer Group subscription revenue was $6.56 billion, which represents 14% year-over-year growth, or 13% in constant currency.
•Business Professionals & Consumers subscription revenue was $1.91 billion, which represents 16% year-over-year growth, or 15% in constant currency.
•Creative & Marketing Professionals subscription revenue was $4.65 billion, which represents 13% year-over-year growth, or 12% in constant currency.

Each of the forward-looking statements we make in this press release involves risks, uncertainties and assumptions based on information available to us as of the date of this press release. Such risks and uncertainties, many of which relate to matters beyond our control, could cause actual results to differ materially from these forward-looking statements. Factors that might cause or contribute to such differences include, but are not limited to: failure to innovate effectively and meet customer needs; failure to compete effectively; issues relating to development and use of AI; damage to our reputation or brands; failure to realize the anticipated benefits of acquisitions, investments or other strategic transactions; failure to recruit and retain key personnel; service interruptions or failures in information technology systems by us or third parties; security incidents; failure to effectively develop, manage and maintain our sales channels or critical third-party business relationships; risks associated with being a multinational corporation and adverse macroeconomic and geopolitical conditions; complex sales cycles; litigation, regulatory inquiries, investigations and other actions; changes in, and compliance with, global laws and regulations, including those related to information security and privacy; failure to protect our intellectual property; changes in tax regulations; complex government procurement processes; risks related to fluctuations in or the timing of revenue recognition from our subscription offerings; fluctuations in foreign currency exchange rates; impairment charges; our existing and future debt obligations; catastrophic events; and fluctuations in our stock price. Adobe Announces Anil Chakravarthy to Become President and CEO
and Shantanu Narayen to Become Executive Chair on December 1, 2026
SAN JOSE, Calif.--(BUSINESS WIRE)--Adobe (Nasdaq: ADBE) — Adobe's Board of Directors today announced that Anil Chakravarthy, president of Adobe’s Customer Experience Orchestration business and worldwide field operations, will become Adobe’s next president and chief executive officer and join the Board of Directors effective December 1, 2026. Shantanu Narayen will transition to executive chair and work closely with Chakravarthy to ensure a smooth transition and support Adobe’s ongoing transformation.
“Adobe’s opportunity ahead is limitless with our track record in creating new market categories and world-class products. Anil is an experienced transformational leader who leads with values, integrity and a deep knowledge of our business. He has a proven record of building and delivering category-defining products that serve our broad range of customers,” said Narayen. “I could not be more confident that Anil is the right person to lead Adobe's growth in an AI-driven era and look forward to working closely with him in my new role as executive chair.”
Frank Calderoni, Lead Independent Director of Adobe, who led the special committee overseeing the selection process said, “The Board has unanimously determined that Anil is the right leader for Adobe’s next chapter of growth. Over the last six and a half years, he has transformed and expanded Adobe’s Customer Experience Orchestration business and worldwide field operations through innovation-led growth, developing and retaining talent and carrying forward Adobe's culture and values. We conducted a rigorous selection process resulting in the appointment of an outstanding CEO.”
Chakravarthy said, “I am deeply honored to have been chosen to lead Adobe during this pivotal moment. I'm energized by the opportunity to fuel growth and drive Adobe's leadership in the next era of agentic software for creativity, productivity and customer experience. Adobe has a history of building the future — not just through our technology, but through our people and our commitment to customers. Thanks to Shantanu's exceptional leadership in transforming Adobe's business model over the decades, we are well positioned to achieve Adobe's next chapter of growth. I want to thank the Board for the confidence they've placed in me. I look forward to working closely with our employees, Shantanu and the Board of Directors to continue serving our customers and transforming Adobe in the era of AI.”
Chakravarthy joined Adobe in January 2020 as executive vice president and general manager leading the Digital Experience business. In September 2020, he took on the additional responsibility of leading Adobe’s worldwide field operations serving enterprise customers with the full portfolio of Adobe’s products including creativity and productivity. In December 2021, he was promoted to president of Digital Experience and worldwide field operations.
Under Chakravarthy’s leadership, Adobe has become an industry leader in Customer Experience Orchestration solutions. He has led the development of market-leading products including Adobe CX Enterprise, GenStudio and Brand Visibility, which are category-defining products using the power of AI to deliver breakthrough customer experiences. He has been instrumental in scaling Adobe Experience Platform and the introduction of new product innovations like CX Enterprise Coworker. He successfully championed the acquisitions and integration of Workfront and Semrush.
Prior to his current role, Chakravarthy served as CEO for four years at Informatica, a global leader in enterprise cloud data management. He originally joined Informatica in 2013 as executive vice president. Before joining Informatica, Chakravarthy acquired broad experience in the technology industry through executive roles at Symantec, VeriSign and McKinsey & Company. Chakravarthy received a Bachelor of Technology in Computer Science and Engineering from the Institute of Technology, Varanasi, India and a Masters of Science and Ph.D from the Massachusetts Institute of Technology.

text: Wall Street Has Its Eyes on Adobe. Here’s Where the Stock Could Be Headed. Adobe is down nearly 28% this year yet still beating earnings estimates and raising guidance, which raises an uncomfortable question about whether the market has gotten the AI disruption story completely wrong. Published October 19, 2026, 8:00am ET · 3 min read Price Targets desk. Editor: Vandita Jadeja. Adobe is a multinational software company best known for its Photoshop and Acrobat. © Adobe logo (CC by 2.0) by midiman The 24/7 Wall St. price target for Adobe (NASDAQ:ADBE | ADBE Price Prediction) is $294.54 over the next 12 months. With shares trading at $252.88, that works out to 16.5% upside. The stock gets a buy rating with high confidence. Price Target from 24/7 Wall St. Adobe’s growth is holding up and guidance keeps rising, yet the stock is priced as if its business is shrinking. That gap drives the call. At a forward P/E of about 9x, the market has already priced in a lot of fear about AI disruption. The open question is whether Adobe can turn rapid AI adoption into a clear acceleration in annual recurring revenue (ARR). We think the current price leaves enough room for that to work. Shares gained 5.07% today and 8.64% over the past week. Shares remain down 4.79% over the past month and 27.75% year to date. The stock sits 30.5% below its 52-week high of $363.70 and 33% above its low of $190.12. The bounce came right after a widely read Barron’s report on a downgrade to Sell over growth concerns. The latest results were solid. Fiscal Q3 revenue rose 12.9% to $6.76 billion, ahead of the $6.70 billion consensus. Non-GAAP EPS of $6.13 beat the $6.09 estimate. Management also raised full-year non-GAAP EPS guidance to $24.45 to $24.50. Leadership is changing too: Anil Chakravarthy becomes CEO on December 1, and Shantanu Narayen stays on as executive chair. Adobe’s AI-first ARR now exceeds $650 million and is growing more than 150% a year. Firefly ARR rose 40% quarter over quarter. Creative freemium users passed 100 million, up more than 70%. Adobe has also held off on pricing actions to build its user base first, which gives it room to raise prices later. Capital returns add support: Adobe bought back 9.5 million shares last quarter and has $24.55 billion left under its authorization. Of the analysts covering the stock, 11 rate it Buy or Strong Buy, and the consensus target is $272.31. The bull case is $326.20. Remaining performance obligations grew just 8%, and analysts pressed management on net new ARR. Five analysts rate the stock Sell or Strong Sell. Net income rose only 3.1%. On the other side of the ledger, free cash flow grew 14.68%, and much of the profit lag reflects planned investment in freemium growth. The bear case is at $254.03.
